title: Sales Enablement Playbook: Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Decks, Pricing & Security FAQ
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook consolidates standardized positioning, competitive brief guidance, an executable pitch-deck outline, pricing negotiation guidance, exemplar case studies, and a prospect-facing security FAQ for Redwood Inference sales teams and field reps. Use this as the canonical source when preparing customer-facing materials for enterprise and mid-market opportunities.

Audience: Account executives, solutions engineers, sales enablement, growth marketing, and channel partners.

Key outcomes: consistent messaging, faster deal cycles, reduced risk in security conversations, and repeatable pricing concessions tied to committed usage models.

1) One-line positioning

Redwood Inference: A developer-first inference platform that delivers predictable, low-latency, and cost-efficient LLM serving across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

2) Problem statement (what prospects tell us)

- Rising inference costs and unpredictable latency under production load.
- Difficulty scaling models across regions and hardware types while preserving SLAs.
- Security and compliance concerns for regulated data and on-prem needs.
- Operational burden of patching, kernel selection, and kv-cache tuning.

3) Core value pillars (three messaging pillars + proof points)

Pillar A — Predictable performance and reliability
- Messaging: Single API, consistent SLOs across hosted, dedicated, and private modes.
- Proof points: 99.95% uptime SLA for Dedicated, 95th percentile tail latency targets published per model.
- Supporting collateral: runtime benchmark matrix (link), latency dashboard sample.

Pillar B — Cost-aware serving and optimization
- Messaging: Intelligent batching, automated prefix caching, and quantization profiles reduce per-token cost without sacrificing quality.
- Proof points: Typical customers see 30–60% unit cost reduction vs self-hosted baseline; Redwood Optimize report template included.
- Supporting collateral: Cost impact calculator (spreadsheet link), representative pricing bands.

Pillar C — Flexible deployments and enterprise controls
- Messaging: Hosted API for rapid onboarding; Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput; Private VPC/on-prem for regulatory requirements with KMS/HSM integration.
- Proof points: Customer X moved to Dedicated and maintained throughput at 2x peak load with 0% downtime during rollout.

4) Tactical messaging by persona

- ML Engineer: "Ship models faster with predictable latency and automatic KV caching; avoid kernel tuning headaches."
- Platform/Infra: "Consolidate model serving into one runtime with autoscaling, tracing hooks, and per-route cost breakdowns."
- Security/Compliance: "Private deployments with customer-managed networking, KMS integration, and full audit logs—SOC2-ready evidence pack available."
- Product Manager / PMM: "Deliver ML features with predictable unit economics and safe fallbacks to maintain UX during incidents."

5) Competitive brief (short form)

Top competitors: Major cloud vendor managed endpoints, LLM API providers, and self-hosted inference runtimes.

Competitive comparison (high-level table)

| Feature / Competitor | Redwood Inference | Cloud Managed Endpoints | LLM API Provider | Open-source Runtime + Ops |
|----------------------|-------------------|-------------------------|------------------|--------------------------|
| Deployment modes     | Hosted / Dedicated / Private | Hosted / Regional | Hosted only | Self-hosted only |
| Developer experience | Simple API + SDKs, benchmarking profiles | Simple API, less model catalog detail | Simple API, limited ops | Full control, high ops burden |
| Cost controls        | Batching, caching, quantization profiles | Limited | Usage-based discounts only | Variable, depends on ops |
| Enterprise controls  | KMS/HSM, VPC, audit logs, SLAs | VPC in some cases | Limited | Depends on implementer |
| Reliability          | Smart routing, fallbacks, SLAs | Regional failover | Dependent on provider | Operator-managed |

Competitive talking points:
- Against cloud-managed endpoints: emphasize unit economics, model catalog and verification, and cross-environment parity (same API for private and hosted).
- Against LLM API providers: emphasize predictability at scale and enterprise controls (Dedicated, VPC, SLAs).
- Against open-source runtime + ops: emphasize lower TCO when accounting for engineering time and optimizations delivered by Redwood.

6) Pitch deck outline (recommended 10–12 slide flow)

Slide 1 — Title + Hook
- One-liner, ACV target, demo ask

Slide 2 — Customer problem
- Concrete latency/cost/security pain, data points from discovery

Slide 3 — Why now
- Model capabilities + product usage trends increasing inference burden

Slide 4 — Redwood value proposition
- Three pillars (performance, cost, deployment flexibility)

Slide 5 — Product tour (hosted / dedicated / private)
- Bullet list of features by mode; include sample dashboard screenshot

Slide 6 — Architecture + runtime overview
- Simple diagram text: smart router, serving runtime, KV cache, autoscaler; include SLOs (e.g., p95 < 200ms for short generation workloads in Dedicated)

Slide 7 — Security & compliance
- VPC/private control plane, KMS/HSM, audit logs, SOC2 evidence pack, penetration testing cadence

Slide 8 — Pricing model & contract options
- Usage-based tiers, reserved Dedicated capacity, enterprise licensing (see pricing guidance below)

Slide 9 — Case studies / success metrics
- Short bullets with impact (latency, cost reduction, time-to-prod)

Slide 10 — Implementation & onboarding plan
- Recommended timeline (0–30 days: pilot; 30–90 days: production) and owners (SE, CSM)

Slide 11 — Pricing ask & next steps
- Trial terms, POC scope, decision criteria, legal/Security contact details

7) Pricing guidance (sales playbook rules)

Pricing constructs (use these canonical terms when negotiating):
- Hosted API (pay as you go): per-token generation and per-embedding units with tiered volume discounts.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly committed throughput with guaranteed GPU pools; baseline discount vs hosted list in exchange for term commitment.
- Private (Enterprise license): platform fee + support tier + optional on-prem packaging.

Representative pricing bands (example only — use pricing spreadsheet for final quotes):

|| Tier || Typical ARR Range || Discount levers || Notes ||
|| Developer / Startup || <$50k/year || promotional credits, standard list || self-serve onboarding ||
|| Growth || $50k–$500k/year || volume discounts, modest term commitments || consider Dedicated pilot ||
|| Enterprise || >$500k/year || reserved capacity pricing, multi-year discounts, enhanced SLAs || include SOC2 evidence, SSO/KMS requirements ||

Negotiation playbook (numbered steps):
1. Start from list pricing and present standard volume tiers.
2. If prospect requests discounts, qualify committed usage (QPS, token volume, retention needs).
3. Offer Dedicated pilot discount for 6–12 month committed throughput if prospect needs predictability.
4. Use on-prem / private as an upsell only after security and compliance qualifiers are satisfied.
5. Engage finance for any >25% discount or non-standard legal terms.

Discount examples (guidance only):
- 10–20% for 12-month committed Dedicated with 3–6 month ramp clause.
- 25–40% for multi-year enterprise commitments with minimum ARR guarantees.

8) Case studies (two short examples for prospect conversations)

Customer A — "FinServe" (virtualized case name)
- Industry: Financial services
- Challenge: Low-latency document summarization at scale with strict audit requirements.
- Solution: Private deployment in customer VPC, KMS for key management, Redwood Optimize quantization profiles to reduce cost while preserving model fidelity.
- Impact: 45% reduction in inference cost, p95 generation time reduced from 850ms to 220ms, passed internal audit with full audit log export.

Customer B — "RetailCo"
- Industry: Retail personalization
- Challenge: Sporadic peak traffic during promotions; unpredictable cloud inference costs and model fallbacks.
- Solution: Dedicated capacity with autoscaling policies and smart routing across regions; automatic fallback to smaller model variants during extreme load.
- Impact: Maintained 99.9% availability during peak promotion windows, 32% reduction in per-session inference cost.

9) Security FAQ for prospects (concise, shareable answers)

Q: How is customer data handled in Hosted mode?
A: In Hosted mode customer requests traverse Redwood runtime; by default data is isolated per account, logs and traces can be configured to omit request payloads. We offer data retention configuration and can disable persistent logging for sensitive use cases.

Q: Do you support VPC / private deployments?
A: Yes. Redwood Private supports a customer-managed VPC with a private control plane, optional on-prem packaging, and SOC2/ISO evidence available upon request.

Q: What key management options are available?
A: KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) are supported for encryption-at-rest and HSM-backed keys can be integrated for private deployments.

Q: How do you handle audit logging and access controls?
A: We provide tenant-scoped audit logs (API calls, config changes), RBAC with SSO/SAML integration, and an exportable audit archive for compliance reviews.

Q: Are you SOC2 / ISO compliant?
A: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II readiness; SOC2 report and other compliance artifacts are available to enterprise customers under NDA.

Q: How do you ensure model outputs do not leak PII?
A: We recommend prompt engineering, output filters, and opt-in redaction policies. For high-risk workloads we support private deployments and do not persist request/response payloads.

Q: What is your incident response posture?
A: Dedicated customers benefit from SLA-backed incident response; we have on-call rotations, incident runbooks, and customer notification templates. We publish incident postmortems internally and provide external comms for major incidents.

10) Implementation & trial checklist (short, actionable)

- Step 0: Discovery call — collect target QPS, average sequence length, model family, SLOs, and compliance requirements.
- Step 1: Sign POC agreement and data processing addendum (if needed).
- Step 2: Pilot (0–30 days) — provide sandbox credentials, run representative traffic, collect telemetry, produce cost projection.
- Step 3: Review and tune — optimize batching, caching, quantization profile and autoscaling settings.
- Step 4: Production rollout (30–90 days) — migrate traffic, enable monitoring dashboards and alerting; schedule post-launch review with CSM.

Ownership: SEs run the pilot, Account Execs drive commercial terms, CSM owns post-launch success.

12) OKRs & measurement for enablement success

- Reduce average time-to-first-production (pilot -> prod) from 45 days to 30 days by EOY.
- Increase win rate for deals requiring private deployment by 15% over baseline.
- Decrease average discounting on Dedicated deals to <20% through better qualification and standardized pilots.

13) Next steps and playbook governance

- Quarterly review cycle: sales enablement owns updates; Product and Security contribute changes after each major release or audit.
- For any changes to pricing guidance or SLAs, notify Finance and Legal and capture approval records.

Appendix: Example CLI for quick smoke test (SE playbook)

# Example: run a sample generation against the hosted sandbox API (replace API_KEY)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer API_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-qa-1","input":"Summarize recent performance improvements and expected costs for a 1M token/month workload."}'

JSON response includes latency_ms, token_count, and cost_estimate fields which should be validated against the pricing calculator during the pilot.
